risks.note: The auditors report that 'the Company's current liabilities exceed the current assets by Rs. 42,432.87 lakhs as at March 31, 2026' and that, in the absence of sufficient appropriate audit evidence to support the Company's ability to meet its obligations, a material uncertainty exists that may cast significant doubt on the entity's ability to continue as a going concern - and that the standalone financial statements neither use another acceptable basis of accounting nor adequately disclose the matter.
risks.risk: Material uncertainty over the Company's ability to continue as a going concern

risks.note: The Company owns Hotel Hyatt Regency in Mumbai, which is 'in shut condition as on date'. The MD&A states 'the operations of the Company are not yet started after coming out from CIRP', and the Company employed only two people during the year (the Company Secretary and the Chief Financial Officer). Restart is contingent on completing a physical verification and evaluation of PPE before commencing operation, with no date given.
risks.risk: The Company's own hotel is shut and generates no operations

risks.note: Novak Hotels Private Limited ('Saraf Group') advanced amounts to the Company under a framework agreement entered into between the promoters and the Saraf Group during the insolvency resolution process, and the agreement gives the Saraf Group an option to acquire Hyatt Regency, Mumbai. The Board obtained shareholder approval to create a charge/lien over the hotel to secure those amounts, and Novak's own audited accounts describe them as advances for acquiring the hotel - so the auditors are 'unable to state if the classification of amounts received is' appropriate. The Company's single owned asset is therefore encumbered and potentially subject to transfer.
risks.risk: The Saraf Group's option to acquire Hyatt Regency, Mumbai, and the unresolved classification of the funding it advanced

risks.note: 'The Company has neither provided us with proper records showing full particulars, including quantitative details and situation of property, plant and equipment nor has provided us with the information regarding the physical verification of property, plant and equipment. Therefore, we are unable to comment on the existence of the property, plant' - the auditors' inability bears directly on the carrying value of the Company's principal asset.
risks.risk: Fixed-asset records and physical verification are absent, so the existence of the property, plant and equipment cannot be confirmed

risks.note: 'Outstanding recoverable/payables balances with the Government Authorities are subject to reconciliation with the statutory records and consequential adjustment, if any', and in the absence of complete period details of statutory dues payable the auditors are unable to comment on the adequacy of interest expense recognised on those dues - an open, potentially growing liability of unknown size.
risks.risk: Unreconciled statutory dues and government-authority balances

risks.note: 'During the period under review, the Company engaged in only one segment of Hotel Business'. All consolidated earnings arise from one subsidiary, Aria Hotels, which owns one hotel - the JW Marriott at New Delhi Aerocity - while the Company's own asset is one shut hotel in Mumbai. There is no diversification of property, brand, geography or format to absorb a shock at either site.

The Company was 'revived on 9th January, 2024 since than the Management is busy with doing pending compliances with respect of BSE and NSE Stock Exchange and other concerned Authorities.' Suspension of trading was only revoked after applications to both exchanges, and management bandwidth remains absorbed by the compliance backlog rather than by operations.
risks.risk: Compliance and listing-status overhang carried over from insolvency

risks.note: The MD&A's Risks and Concerns section flags a tight labour market and staff shortages that can compromise service quality, rising operational costs for food, utilities and wages that directly compress margins, competition from short-term rental models such as Airbnb that alter pricing structures, reputational exposure to negative social-media reviews, and data-privacy/cybersecurity risk from guest data. It also flags the Israel-Iran conflict feeding oil prices and inflation, to which India is 'particularly sensitive because it imports most of its crude oil', and a consequently cautious RBI on rate cuts.
risks.risk: Cost, labour and demand risks management flags for the hotel business
